region: Pacific Oceania — Micronesia, Polynesia & Hawaii
description: Lives in the white-water surge zone of exposed outer reefs, grazing filamentous algae from rock. The orange teardrop around the tail spine grows larger with age.

region: Indian Ocean — East Africa to the Andaman Sea & Bali
description: Forms large grazing aggregations on shallow reef flats and outer slopes of the Indian Ocean. Often intolerant of other tangs and prone to marine ich in captivity.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia & the Philippines to southern Japan
description: A chocolate-brown grazer with a white band running from the eye to the mouth and orange stripes along the bases of the dorsal and anal fins. Lives on shallow, wave-swept reef flats.

region: Indo-Pacific to the eastern Pacific — Cocos-Keeling to Hawaii & Mexico
description: Sold as the Gold Rim Tang for the thin yellow lines along its fin bases; a small white cheek spot sits below the eye. Grazes algae on clear-water outer reefs.

region: Western Atlantic — New York & Bermuda to Brazil, incl. Gulf & Caribbean; Ascension
description: Juveniles are bright yellow and pass through a blue-with-yellow-tail stage before turning all blue. Adults graze turf algae in roving schools that swamp territorial damselfish.

region: Indo-Pacific — East Africa to the Marquesas & Ryukyu Islands
description: Holds feeding territories and harems on surge-battered reef crests, chasing off other grazers. Its tail spine is venomous and it is one of the most aggressive surgeonfishes in aquaria.

region: Red Sea & Arabian Gulf
description: Defends algae gardens on the outer edges of Red Sea reefs where waves break. Its thin black lines and orange tail spine make it striking, but it is among the most aggressive tangs in captivity.

region: Western & central Pacific, eastern Indian Ocean
description: Adults bear an orange bar outlined in dark blue behind the eye; juveniles are plain yellow. Feeds on diatom and detritus films over sand and rubble.

region: Indo-Pacific — Seychelles to the Marquesas & southern Japan
description: Juveniles mimic Centropyge angelfishes (lemonpeel-yellow or half-black pearlscale patterns) and are sold as Mimic Tangs. Adults turn brown with an orange patch around the gill opening and a yellow-edged tail.

region: Indo-Pacific incl. Red Sea & Hawaii
description: One of the most abundant surgeonfishes on shallow reef flats, also called the Lavender Tang; tiny orange spots dot its head. Gathers in huge spawning aggregations at dusk.

region: Indo-Pacific & eastern Pacific — East Africa to Panama
description: Forms large roving schools that overwhelm territorial damselfish to graze their algae. Pale greenish-white with narrow black vertical bars, the first through the eye and a short one on the tail stalk.

region: Indo-Pacific — East Africa to the Tuamotus
description: Named for the black elongate streak behind the eye; a second black streak runs forward from the tail spine. Feeds on algal and detrital films over sand next to reefs.

region: Indo-Pacific — East Africa to Hawaii & the Line Islands
description: Tan with fine wavy blue lines, a yellow-orange band behind the eye and a blue tail sprinkled with black spots. Grazes diatom and detritus films off sand, and grows large.

region: Indo-Pacific incl. Red Sea
description: A plankton-feeding surgeonfish that schools in midwater along steep, often turbid reef slopes. It can switch from dark brown to pale blue in seconds; two yellow lines run forward from the eye.

region: Atlantic — Massachusetts to Brazil incl. Caribbean; West Africa
description: Grey-brown with about ten narrow dark vertical bars and a dark-edged tail spine. Grazes turf algae in mixed schools with Atlantic blue tangs and ocean surgeons.

region: Western South Atlantic — Brazil, Ascension & St Helena
description: A plain tan-grey Atlantic surgeonfish with a pale band around the tail base and a pale-edged, deeply concave tail; Caribbean and Gulf populations are now treated as A. tractus. Grazes algae over reef and seagrass edges.

region: Indian Ocean — East Africa to Sri Lanka & western Indonesia
description: Brown with two dark, blue-edged dashes behind the eye and a blue-ringed black patch around the tail spine. Juveniles are orange-yellow.

region: Indo-Pacific & eastern Pacific
description: The largest Acanthurus: purplish-grey with yellow pectoral fins and a yellow patch in front of the eye. Feeds on films of diatoms and detritus over sand; mainly a public-aquarium fish.

region: Indo-Pacific — East Africa to Hawaii & the Tuamotus
description: Dark grey-brown with a yellow streak behind the eye and a white ring around the base of the tail. Grazes algal films off sand and dead coral.

region: Indo-Pacific — East Africa to Hawaii & the Marquesas
description: A plankton-picking surgeonfish that hovers in midwater along drop-offs instead of grazing rock. Uniform chocolate brown with a contrasting white tail.

region: Pacific (antitropical) — Hawaii, southern Japan, Marianas, Polynesia & Easter Island
description: Brown with a white-edged dark bar curving down behind the eye and a pale ring before the tail. Grazes algae in schools on shallow, surge-swept rocky reefs, mostly in subtropical waters.

region: Indo-Pacific — Mauritius to Hawaii & the Tuamotus
description: Lives in the turbulent white water of reef fronts, where its white spots may blend with bubbles. Dark brown with two white bars and yellow pelvic fins.

region: Indo-West Pacific — East Africa to Samoa
description: Named for the orange ring ("socket") around its tail spine; otherwise dark grey-brown with a pale band at the base of the tail. Grazes algal and detrital films on sand and rubble next to reefs.

region: Red Sea & Gulf of Aden
description: Red Sea sister species of the epaulette surgeonfish: dark brown to black with a black streak behind the eye and a white band across the base of the tail.

region: Pacific — Indonesia to Hawaii & the Tuamotus
description: Raises enormous dorsal and anal fins to look twice its size when threatened. Tan and brown vertical bands cover the body, and the head is dotted with pale yellow spots.

region: Red Sea & Indian Ocean — East Africa to India & Indonesia
description: Indian Ocean counterpart of the Pacific sailfin, with fine yellow vertical lines between its dark bars and a head covered in pale spots. Juveniles often hide among branching corals.

region: Indo-Pacific — East Africa to the Tuamotus & southern Japan
description: Also called the Brown or Two-tone Tang: tan in front, darkening to chocolate toward the tail, with a white tail spine. Small groups graze filamentous algae on reef slopes.

region: Red Sea, Gulf of Aden & Arabian Gulf
description: Deep purple-blue with a bright yellow tail and pectoral fins and fine dark speckles on the head. Grazes algae on Red Sea reefs and is notably intolerant of other Zebrasoma.

region: Western Indian Ocean — Mozambique, Madagascar, Mauritius & Réunion
description: Dark brownish-black peppered with white spots and finished with a yellow tail. Restricted to the western Indian Ocean and one of the most expensive tangs in the trade.

region: South Pacific — Society, Tuamotu, Marquesas, Line & Pitcairn Islands
description: An all-black Zebrasoma with a markedly long snout from remote Polynesian islands; the snout lengthens with age. Rare and costly in the trade.

region: Hawaiian Islands & Johnston Atoll
description: Uses comb-like bristle teeth to brush diatoms and detritus off rock rather than biting algae. Brown with fine blue lines and a bright yellow ring around the eye.

region: Western central Pacific — Indonesia & the Philippines to the Solomons
description: A bristletooth from sheltered lagoon reefs, named for the Gulf of Tomini in Sulawesi. Grey-brown with orange-red rear dorsal and anal fins edged in white.

region: Pacific — Hawaii, Micronesia & Polynesia
description: Juveniles are orange with blue chevron lines; adults turn almost black with fine olive pinstripes. Brushes diatom film off reef rock with flexible bristle teeth.

region: Indo-Pacific — East Africa to the Tuamotus
description: Brown with fine blue lines, a blue ring around the eye and a small black spot at the rear base of both the dorsal and anal fins. Juveniles have a yellow tail.

region: Indo-Pacific incl. Red Sea
description: One of the most abundant reef surgeonfishes, sweeping detritus and diatoms from dead coral. Dark olive-brown with many thin blue-grey lines and tiny orange dots on the head.

region: Indian Ocean — East Africa to the Andaman Sea
description: Indian Ocean twin of the Kole Tang: dark grey-brown with fine blue dots and a golden ring around the eye. Juveniles are sometimes bright yellow.

region: Pacific — Indonesia & southern Japan to Hawaii & the Tuamotus
description: A hornless unicornfish with a yellow-edged dark face mask, orange lips and two orange keeled plates on each side of the tail stalk. Browses leafy brown algae; males grow trailing tail streamers.

region: Indian Ocean & Red Sea — East Africa to Bali
description: The Indian Ocean sister of the orangespine unicornfish, sold as the Blonde Naso for its yellow-orange dorsal fin. Grazes leafy brown algae over reef flats.

region: Indo-Pacific incl. Red Sea — East Africa to Hawaii & the Marquesas
description: Adults grow a short bony horn on the forehead and carry two blue keeled plates on the tail stalk. Browses tough brown algae in schools on shallow reefs; a public-aquarium species.

region: Indo-Pacific — East Africa to the Marquesas & southern Japan
description: Covered in blue dots and vertical blue lines that brighten instantly when it visits a cleaning station; adults develop a bulbous snout. Feeds on zooplankton in midwater off reef slopes.

region: Indo-Pacific — Red Sea & East Africa to Hawaii & the Marquesas
description: Adults grow a long, tapering horn that projects forward over the mouth. Juveniles graze algae, while adults switch to feeding on zooplankton in midwater along reef slopes.

region: Indo-Pacific — Red Sea & East Africa to Hawaii & the Marquesas
description: A slender, hornless unicornfish that schools above steep outer reef slopes feeding on zooplankton. Males can flash a pale blue courtship pattern within seconds.

region: Eastern Pacific — Gulf of California to El Salvador
description: Grey peppered with black spots, with a bright yellow tail and a row of black bony plates along the tail stalk. Travels the rocky reefs of the Gulf of California in large grazing schools.

region: Eastern Pacific — Costa Rica to Ecuador, Cocos & Galápagos Islands
description: Grey with two dark bars across the head and a yellow tail; the black keeled plates on its tail stalk give it its name. Forms large grazing schools around the Galápagos.

region: Southwest Pacific — eastern Australia, Lord Howe Island & New Caledonia
description: Grey with scattered yellow spots and short yellow lines, and three or four black plates on the tail stalk. A subtropical grazer often seen in schools on rocky reefs around Sydney.

region: Eastern Australia — southern Queensland to New South Wales
description: A large, plain grey to grey-brown surgeonfish with a row of five or six black bony plates along the tail stalk. Schools over shallow rocky reefs and kelp edges.

region: Northwest Pacific — southern Japan, Taiwan & southern China
description: A grey sawtail with four or five black keeled plates on the tail stalk, abundant on rocky reefs of southern Japan. Schools graze algae in the cool, temperate-subtropical water.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia & the Philippines to New Caledonia & the Marshall Islands
description: Pairs browse algae among branching corals; the fin spines are venomous. When frightened or asleep it fades to a mottled brown and raises its dorsal spines.

region: Western Pacific — Philippines, Ryukyu Islands & Great Barrier Reef
description: Identical to the common foxface except for a black blotch on the upper flank; some authors treat it as a colour form of S. vulpinus. Browses algae in pairs among corals.

region: Eastern Indian Ocean — Andaman Sea (Thailand & Myanmar)
description: Andaman Sea endemic with the foxface's black-and-white face plus a broad black saddle across the middle of the back. Pairs graze algae among corals.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia to the Great Barrier Reef & Fiji
description: Yellow overlaid with wavy blue lines and two dark diagonal bars on the head. Lives in pairs on coastal reefs, grazing algae and seagrass.

region: Indo-West Pacific — India & Sri Lanka to the Philippines & northern Australia
description: Yellow with blue-spotted head and back and two dark, blue-edged diagonal bars across the head. Pairs graze algae on coastal reefs and around mangroves.

region: Indian Ocean incl. Red Sea — East Africa to the Andaman Sea
description: Pale grey-white densely covered with dark brown spots, with a bright yellow margin to the tail and rear dorsal fin. Pairs patrol coral reefs grazing algae.

region: Eastern Indian Ocean & western Pacific — Andaman Sea to the Philippines & Palau
description: Blue-grey with dense golden-orange spots and a bright yellow blotch below the rear of the dorsal fin. Tolerates brackish estuaries and mangroves and is farmed for food in Southeast Asia.

region: Indo-West Pacific — Seychelles to New Caledonia
description: Golden yellow-orange covered in small blue spots, with a dark triangular patch below the eye. Lives in pairs among live coral, grazing algae.

region: Eastern Indian Ocean & western Pacific — Cocos-Keeling to Kiribati
description: Yellow with blue wavy lines and spots, and a dark diagonal mask running through the eye. Pairs live among corals on clear lagoon and seaward reefs.

region: Southwest Pacific — Fiji & New Caledonia
description: Dark chocolate-brown over the front two-thirds and bright yellow at the rear and tail. Restricted to Fiji and New Caledonia, where pairs browse algae among coral.

region: Eastern Indian Ocean & western Pacific — Sri Lanka to New Caledonia & Vanuatu
description: Blue-grey with wavy golden lines and a yellow blotch below the rear dorsal fin. Forms schools in shallow lagoons and seagrass beds, grazing algae.

region: Western Pacific — Ryukyu Islands to the Great Barrier Reef & Samoa
description: Dusky blue-grey densely covered with small golden-orange spots. Adults live in pairs on coral reefs, grazing algae.

region: Indo-West Pacific — Arabian Gulf to Indonesia & Vanuatu
description: Blue-grey with pale spots on the upper body that turn into wavy lines lower down, and a dark tail. Schools in turbid coastal waters and estuaries.

region: Indo-Pacific & eastern Pacific — East Africa to Mexico
description: Sole member of its family, with a tubular snout, broad black bands and a long white dorsal streamer. Feeds largely on sponges and tunicates, which makes it notoriously hard to keep.

region: Pacific Oceania — Palau & the Marshall Islands to Hawaii & the Marquesas
description: Brilliant red-orange with four or five black bars and blue-black-tipped dorsal and anal fins. Lives in small harems among rubble and coral heads; like all dwarf angels it begins life female.

region: Indo-West Pacific — East Africa to Samoa & southern Japan
description: Bright yellow front and tail with a royal-blue rear body and a blue saddle over the eye. Forms harems in rubble zones and lagoons.

region: Indo-Pacific — East Africa to the Tuamotus & southern Japan
description: Orange flanks crossed by fine dark blue-purple bars, under a deep-blue back and fins. Lives among rubble and coral on lagoon and outer reefs; among the hardiest dwarf angels.

region: Eastern Indian Ocean & western Pacific — Sri Lanka to Indonesia & northwest Australia
description: Pale grey crossed by fine orange vertical lines, darkening to black at the rear, with a gold ring around the eye. Juveniles of the surgeonfish Acanthurus tristis mimic its colours.

region: Western Pacific — southern Japan, Taiwan & the Philippines
description: Rusty orange-brown peppered with small dark spots, with electric-blue edges on the dorsal and anal fins. Lives in rubble and crevices on shallow reefs.

region: Indo-Pacific — Cocos-Keeling to the Line, Marquesas & Ducie islands
description: Lemon-yellow with electric-blue rings around the eyes and blue edges on the gill cover and fins. Notorious for nipping clam mantles and large-polyp stony corals.

region: Pacific — Taiwan & the Philippines to the Tuamotus
description: All yellow, lacking the blue eye ring and fin edges of the lemonpeel; some show a dusky smudge behind the eye. Lives among rubble on outer reef slopes.

region: Hawaiian Islands & Johnston Atoll
description: Hawaiian endemic with an orange-red head and forebody grading into a dark blue rear, all crossed by fine wavy dark lines. Shy, staying close to coral rubble.

region: Western Atlantic — Bermuda, Florida, Gulf of Mexico & Caribbean
description: Among the smallest marine angelfishes: deep blue with a yellow-orange face and chest and a blue eye ring. Lives among rubble and coral heads, mostly on deeper reef slopes.

region: Western Indian Ocean — East Africa, Madagascar & the Seychelles
description: Deep blue with an orange-yellow head and back and a clear tail. A small, comparatively peaceful dwarf angel of rubble slopes.

region: Western Atlantic — southern Caribbean to Brazil
description: Blue body with an orange band running from the snout along the back; unlike the African flameback its tail is blue. Lives in rubble on deeper reefs.

region: Western Pacific — Christmas Island to the Marshall Islands & Vanuatu
description: Pale cream at the front blending to black at the rear, with an orange spot behind the gill cover. Commonly hybridizes with Eibl's and lemonpeel angelfishes.

region: Western Pacific — Christmas Island to New Caledonia & southern Japan
description: Blue-black with a single white vertical blotch on the flank, likened to a keyhole, and yellow pelvic fins. Lives among rubble on lagoon and outer reefs.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia & the Philippines to the Solomon Islands & GBR
description: Entirely jet-black, a secretive dwarf angel of rubble slopes and coral thickets. Less inclined to nip corals than most of its relatives.

region: Indian Ocean incl. Red Sea — East Africa to the Andaman Sea
description: Dark brown with faint vertical bars, a black spot behind the gill and blue-edged fins. Abundant in rubble and coral crevices and very hardy in aquaria.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia to the Great Barrier Reef & Samoa
description: Orange-gold covered in fine dark vertical lines, with thin blue fin edges. Extremely shy, rarely leaving deep crevices on rubble slopes.

region: Northwest Pacific — southern Japan, Ogasawara Islands & Midway
description: Orange head and forebody grading into a blue rear, sprinkled with blue spots, and an orange-yellow tail. One of the largest Centropyge, from cool subtropical reefs.

region: Eastern Indian Ocean — Christmas & Cocos-Keeling Islands
description: Yellow front and tail with a royal-blue rear body and a blue ring around the eye. Known only from Christmas and Cocos-Keeling islands.

region: South Atlantic — Ascension Island
description: Ascension Island endemic: deep blue with a yellow-orange band running from the snout over the back and into the dorsal fin. Lives among rubble and rocky reef.

region: Hawaiian Islands & Johnston Atoll
description: A small Hawaiian dwarf angel, orange with a darker rear, a dark spot behind the gill and blue-lined dorsal and anal fins. Lives in rubble on deeper reef slopes.

region: Western Pacific — Cocos-Keeling, Palau, Guam & Fiji
description: A deep-reef dwarf angel, yellow with a large blue-violet saddle across the back and dorsal fin and a blue eye ring. Usually found below 30 m in caves on steep walls.

region: South Pacific — Cook Islands (Rarotonga)
description: Lemon-yellow with a large black spot on the upper flank, found on deep walls beyond 100 m; named for the nitrogen narcosis divers risk collecting it. Very rare in the trade.

region: Indian Ocean — Sri Lanka, the Maldives & Andaman Sea
description: Dark blue-black with faint darker lines and contrasting bright yellow pectoral fins. Lives among rubble on reef slopes of the central Indian Ocean.

region: Western Pacific — Mariana & Ogasawara Islands
description: Orange with irregular darker vertical bars and blue-edged dorsal and anal fins, sometimes sold as the Mango Angelfish. Hybridizes with the coral beauty where the two meet in the Mariana Islands.

region: Indo-Pacific — Cocos-Keeling to the Society Islands & southern Japan
description: Pale yellow-white with bold black vertical bars and yellow pelvic fins. Secretive, hiding deep in caves and crevices of reef walls; often slow to feed in aquaria.

region: Western Pacific — southern Japan, Taiwan & the Philippines
description: Golden yellow with a purple-blue back, mask and fins. A deep-reef species living in caves on steep walls, rarely collected.

region: South Pacific — Cook Islands (Rarotonga) & French Polynesia
description: Red-orange with five crisp white vertical bars, living in caves on walls deeper than 50 m. One of the most expensive aquarium fishes ever sold.

region: Western Pacific — Malaysia & Indonesia to Vanuatu & southern Japan
description: A silvery planktivore striped in black that feeds in midwater above steep slopes, unlike most angelfishes. Males are larger and carry a yellow spot on the forehead.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia to Fiji & southern Japan
description: A swallowtail angel with strong sexual dichromatism: females are yellow-backed with black-edged tail lobes, while males are pale blue-grey with fine black bars and a black chest spot.

region: Western & central Pacific — Taiwan & southern Japan to the Tuamotus & New Caledonia
description: Females are pale blue with black-edged dorsal fin and tail lobes and a dark cap; males are bluer with black horizontal lines on the lower flanks. Feeds on plankton along deep walls.

region: Indo-Pacific — Cocos-Keeling & Indonesia to the Marshall & Society Islands
description: Females are silvery-white with black stripes along the back and from eye to tail; males are pale grey with an orange-yellow stripe along the flank and dorsal fin. A deep-water planktivore.

region: Northwest Pacific — southern Japan, Taiwan, Ogasawara Islands & the northern Philippines
description: Males have a yellow-orange head and back and fine black bars on the mid-flank; females are pale grey with a dark cap and black-edged tail lobes. Feeds on plankton on cool subtropical reefs.

region: Hawaiian Islands (mostly Northwestern Hawaiian Islands) & Midway
description: A deep-water Hawaiian endemic: females are white with a black face mask and black pelvic fins, while males have a yellow-orange mask and fin trim. One of the most sought-after angelfishes.

region: Western Indian Ocean & Red Sea — East Africa to the Maldives
description: Males are pale blue-grey with many thin black vertical bars and a black-lined lyre tail; females are plain pale blue with a dark cap and black-edged tail lobes. Harems feed on plankton along deep slopes.

region: Indo-Pacific incl. Red Sea — East Africa to Hawaii & the Tuamotus
description: Adults are striped yellow on blue with a black mask and a dark, blue-edged shoulder patch; juveniles have concentric white rings on blue and transform at 8–12 cm. Grunts audibly when disturbed.

region: Indo-West Pacific — East Africa to New Guinea & southern Japan
description: Orange-brown with arching blue lines across the body and a blue ring behind the gill cover; the tail is white. Lives in pairs or small groups on coastal reefs and around wrecks.

region: Indo-Pacific incl. Red Sea — East Africa to Fiji & southern Japan
description: Named for the juvenile's white semicircles, said to resemble Arabic script; adults turn greenish-brown with blue-edged fins and blue spots on the face. Hardy and adaptable in large aquaria.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia & the Philippines to New Guinea & the Great Barrier Reef
description: Orange-yellow above with blue-spotted scales and a blue-black lower body outlined in electric blue that sweeps from the face to the tail. Lives on coral-rich lagoon reefs.

region: Indo-West Pacific — Maldives to Vanuatu & southern Japan
description: A blue face mesh with a yellow mask over the eyes, yellow pectoral fins and tail, and a black eyespot at the rear of the dorsal fin. Each body scale is edged in yellow.

region: Western Atlantic — Florida & the Bahamas to Brazil; also Ascension & St Paul's Rocks
description: Black with every scale rimmed in gold, a yellow ring around the eye and a yellow bar at the pectoral base. Pairs roam Caribbean reefs feeding on sponges and often approach divers.

region: Western Atlantic — New England & the Bahamas to Brazil, incl. Gulf & Caribbean
description: Plain grey-brown with dark-centred scales, a pale mouth and a white-edged square tail. Often seen in pairs; feeds mainly on sponges but also on algae, tunicates and soft corals.

region: Red Sea, Arabian Gulf & western Indian Ocean to East Africa
description: Deep blue-violet with dark speckles and a broad, irregular yellow bar across the middle of the body; large adults trail long dorsal and anal filaments. Tolerates turbid coastal reefs.

region: Red Sea, Gulf of Aden & East Africa to Zanzibar
description: Dark blue-black with a broad yellow crescent across the mid-flank and a bright yellow tail. Lives on coastal reefs, often around sheltered coral heads in shallow water.

region: Western Indian Ocean — Gulf of Aden & East Africa to Madagascar
description: Dark brown with thin pale curved bars, an orange spot above the gill cover and a yellow tail. Seldom exported and rare in the trade.

region: Indo-West Pacific — Malaysia & Indonesia to the Solomon Islands & southern Japan
description: Yellowish-brown covered in blue dots with six dark vertical bands and a dark head crossed by a white bar behind the eye. Pairs patrol lagoon and coastal reefs, feeding on sponges and tunicates.

region: Eastern Pacific — Gulf of California to Peru
description: Adults are grey-brown with a curved yellow bar behind the head followed by a black bar; juveniles are black with curved yellow and blue bands. Picks at sponges and algae on rocky reefs.

region: Western Indian Ocean — Kenya to South Africa
description: Adults are pale grey-brown in front and dark brown toward the rear, with a pale tail. Lives on rocky and coral reefs of East and South Africa, feeding on sponges and algae.

region: Western Atlantic — Florida & Bermuda to Brazil, incl. Gulf & Caribbean
description: Blue-green with yellow-rimmed scales, an all-yellow tail and a blue-ringed black "crown" on the forehead. Feeds mainly on sponges; hybridizes with the blue angelfish.

region: Western Atlantic — North Carolina & Bermuda to the Gulf of Mexico & Yucatán
description: Blue-grey with yellow-edged dorsal and anal fins and a yellow tail margin, lacking the queen's crown spot. Hybrids with the queen angelfish (the "Townsend" angelfish) occur where both live.

region: Western Atlantic — Georgia & Bermuda to Brazil, incl. Gulf & Caribbean
description: Bright yellow head and tail with a large black rear body. A sponge specialist that rarely adapts to prepared foods.

region: Eastern Pacific — Gulf of California to Peru & the Galápagos
description: Deep blue-black with a single white vertical bar behind the pectoral fin and an orange-yellow tail. Males have white pelvic fins and females yellow; adults sometimes clean parasites from hammerhead sharks.

region: Eastern Pacific — Revillagigedo Islands & the southern tip of Baja California
description: Brilliant orange with a darker brown head and thin blue bars behind the gill. Adults clean parasites from manta rays at Socorro Island; legally collected specimens are among the priciest angelfishes.

region: Indo-West Pacific — East Africa to Samoa & southern Japan
description: Bright yellow with blue lips, a small black spot on the forehead and a broad black edge to the anal fin. A sponge specialist of outer reef slopes.

region: Indian Ocean — East Africa & the Maldives to Sri Lanka & India
description: Cream-grey with dark-edged scales, a black dorsal fin and a yellow tail; also called the Indian Yellowtail Angelfish. Lives in pairs on coral and rocky reefs.

region: Red Sea, Gulf of Aden & Arabian Sea
description: Red Sea counterpart of the cream angelfish: pale with dark-centred scales, a dark face, a yellow spot by the gill opening and a yellow tail. Shy and usually seen near caves.

region: Hawaiian Islands & Johnston Atoll
description: Grey-white with a bold, white-edged black band running from the eye along the back into the dorsal fin. A deep-water Hawaiian endemic that feeds mainly on sponges.

region: Central Pacific — Palau, Kiribati, the Line & Marshall Islands
description: Each scale carries a gold fleck on a dusky blue-grey body, with a yellowish face, blue lips and black-edged dorsal fin. Collected mainly at Christmas Island in Kiribati.

region: Indo-West Pacific — Sri Lanka & the Andaman Sea to the Philippines & northern Australia
description: White front with a black eye bar and a dark rear covered in fine wavy lines, finished with a yellow tail. Lives on silty coastal reefs, picking at sponges and tunicates.

region: Northwest Pacific — southern Japan, Taiwan & southern China
description: Orange-brown with many wavy blue horizontal lines and a bright yellow tail. Lives on rocky and coral reefs in cool subtropical water, feeding on sponges and tunicates.

region: Northern Australia, southern New Guinea & the Aru Islands
description: Dark blue scribbled with fine blue lines, with a yellow band behind the head and a yellow tail; males are more heavily scribbled than females. Lives on coastal reefs and sponge gardens.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia & the Philippines to southern Japan
description: Velvety charcoal-black with a pale greyish face, yellow-trimmed fins and a pale-edged tail. Lives on sponge-rich coastal reefs.

region: Southwest Pacific — Coral Sea, Lord Howe Island, New Caledonia & northern NSW
description: Grey-blue with a vivid yellow face ringed by a blue eye-patch and yellow tail and fin margins. One of the most prized and expensive marine angelfishes.

region: Indo-Pacific incl. Red Sea — East Africa to the Tuamotus
description: Orange-yellow crossed by eight to ten white bars edged in blue-black, with a blue-dotted dorsal fin. A sponge feeder; specimens from the Red Sea and Maldives adapt to captivity far better than Pacific fish.

region: Indo-Pacific incl. Red Sea — East Africa to Hawaii & the Ducie Islands
description: White with crossing dark chevron lines, a yellow rear, a black eye bar and an eyespot under the trailing dorsal filament. A hardy generalist that readily eats Aiptasia anemones.

region: Indo-Pacific — East Africa to Hawaii & the Marquesas
description: Yellow-orange with a white-bordered black mask and a black diagonal band over the shoulder. Largely nocturnal in the wild, resting in groups by day and feeding at night on nudibranchs, worm tentacles and algae.

region: Red Sea & Gulf of Aden
description: Golden yellow with thin orange vertical lines and a blue-grey teardrop patch around the eye. Pairs hover almost motionless beneath table corals for hours.

region: Indo-West Pacific — Arabian Gulf & Maldives to the Philippines & southern Japan
description: Dark brown with a pale checkered scale pattern, white bars across the head and a bright red patch at the base of the tail. Usually seen in pairs or small groups on coral-rich reefs.

region: Indo-Pacific — East Africa to Hawaii & Samoa
description: Tan-yellow with two faint pale bars, a black eye bar and black pelvic fins. One of the few butterflyfishes that readily accepts aquarium foods; feeds on soft corals, algae and plankton.

region: Indo-Pacific — Cocos-Keeling to Hawaii & the Tuamotus
description: Grey with a large white-edged black saddle on the rear back, an orange-red throat and blue lines on the lower flank; adults trail a dorsal filament. Feeds on coral polyps, algae and small invertebrates.

region: Indo-Pacific — Cocos-Keeling to the Tuamotus & southern Japan
description: White with fine vertical lines, two dark saddles across the back, a yellow rear and a black spot on the tail stalk. Usually in pairs, feeding on algae, polyps and small invertebrates.

region: Indian Ocean — East Africa to the Andaman Sea & Bali
description: Indian Ocean twin of the Pacific double-saddle, with darker wedge-shaped saddles and a yellower back and rear. Feeds on algae, coral polyps and worms.

region: Indo-Pacific — East Africa to the Line Islands & southern Japan
description: White with two sets of crossing diagonal lines, a black eye bar and a black band crossing the rear fins and body, with a yellow-and-black-barred tail. A hardy, wide-ranging omnivore.

region: Indian Ocean — Gulf of Oman to Sri Lanka & the Andaman Sea
description: Like the vagabond butterflyfish, but the black area at the rear is much broader, covering the soft dorsal and anal fins. Common on coastal reefs of the northern Indian Ocean.

region: Indo-Pacific — Sri Lanka to the Tuamotus & southern Japan
description: Yellow with a dark net formed by its scale outlines and a black eye bar. Feeds on soft-coral and anemone tentacles and polychaete worms.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia & the Philippines to southern Japan
description: Silvery-white with a dark crosshatched net, a black eye bar, a black nape spot and an orange band across the rear body and tail. Hardy and comparatively easy to feed.

region: Pacific — Taiwan & the Philippines to the Tuamotus & New Caledonia
description: White with grey chevron lines and an orange-yellow rear and tail; a softer-coloured relative of the pearlscale butterflyfish. Feeds on algae, polyps and small invertebrates.

region: Red Sea & Gulf of Aden
description: White with grey chevrons, a yellow-orange eye bar and a vivid red-orange band across the rear and tail. Common in pairs on Red Sea reefs, feeding on algae, polyps and worms.

region: Western Indian Ocean — East Africa, Madagascar & the Mascarenes
description: White with black chevron lines, a black spot on the nape and an orange-red band across the rear body and tail. Lives on outer reef slopes, feeding on polyps and small invertebrates.

region: Hawaiian Islands & Johnston Atoll
description: A lemon-yellow Hawaiian endemic covered in vertical rows of tiny dark dots. Unusually for a butterflyfish, it forms large midwater schools that feed on zooplankton.

region: Indo-Pacific — East Africa to Hawaii & the Tuamotus
description: Pale yellow with rows of small blue-grey spots, a black eye bar and a black-edged anal fin. Common on shallow, exposed reef flats, feeding on polyps, worms and algae.

region: Western Pacific — Christmas Island & Indonesia to the Line Islands & southern Japan
description: Yellow with short dark bars on the back, rows of dark spots below, and an orange eye bar. Lives on coral-rich outer reefs.

region: Western & south Pacific — Palau & the Great Barrier Reef to the Tuamotus
description: Yellow-cream with dotted diagonal lines rising toward the tail, an orange eye bar and an orange band across the tail; also sold as the Sunset Butterflyfish. Feeds on polyps and small invertebrates.

region: Hawaiian Islands & Johnston Atoll
description: A Hawaiian endemic, white with pebble-like brown spots overlain by four faint broad bars. An obligate coral-polyp feeder; pairs defend feeding territories on coral heads.

region: Pacific — Taiwan & the Marianas to Hawaii & the Pitcairn Islands
description: Dark brown upper body with two white spots on each side, a yellow-orange lower body and an orange eye bar. Feeds mainly on the polyps of Pocillopora corals on shallow, exposed reefs.

region: Indo-Pacific — Sri Lanka to Hawaii & the Marquesas
description: White with six slanting orange stripes, black bars on the face and black-edged yellow fins. An obligate feeder on coral polyps and mucus that rarely adapts to aquarium foods.

region: Indo-Pacific — East Africa to the Line Islands & southern Japan
description: Blue-white with bold curved black lines sweeping across the body and yellow-edged fins; also called the Scrawled Butterflyfish. Feeds exclusively on coral polyps.

region: Indo-Pacific incl. Red Sea — East Africa to Samoa & southern Japan
description: White with thin oblique black lines, a black back, yellow fins and a black spot on the tail stalk. Feeds mostly on soft and stony coral polyps.

region: Indo-Pacific incl. Red Sea — East Africa to Hawaii & the Tuamotus
description: An elongate white butterflyfish marked with black chevron lines and a dark, yellow-edged tail. Aggressively guards a single table Acropora colony whose polyps it eats.

region: Pacific — Andaman Sea & Indonesia to Hawaii & the Tuamotus
description: Yellow-tan with fine purple-blue lines, a black eye bar edged in yellow and an orange-red anal fin; the Pacific twin of the Indian Ocean redfin butterflyfish. An obligate coral feeder.

region: Western Pacific — Cocos-Keeling & Indonesia to Fiji & southern Japan
description: Triangular in profile, with white-edged chevrons on a purple-grey body and black eye bars; also called the Baroness Butterflyfish. Feeds almost exclusively on Acropora polyps.

region: Pacific — Ryukyu Islands & the Philippines to Hawaii & the Pitcairn Islands
description: Black with pale-centred scales forming a mesh, a pale bar behind the eye and a red band on the rear anal fin; also called the Mailed Butterflyfish. Feeds on coral polyps on exposed reefs.

region: Indo-Pacific — East Africa to Hawaii & the Pitcairn Islands
description: Yellow above and white below, with a black teardrop spot on the upper flank that trails downward and a black eye bar. Feeds on soft and stony corals, using strong jaws to bite off coral tissue.

region: Eastern Indian Ocean & western Pacific — Christmas Island to Tonga & southern Japan
description: Bright yellow with a large oval black spot beneath the dorsal fin and a black eye bar; also called the Ovalspot Butterflyfish. Feeds on coral polyps and small invertebrates.

region: Western Pacific — Andaman Sea to Fiji & southern Japan
description: Yellow with an elongate blue blotch on the upper flank, an orange-edged eye bar and a white-ringed black spot on the tail stalk. Feeds exclusively on coral polyps.

region: Indo-Pacific — East Africa to the Pitcairn Islands & southern Japan
description: Yellow with a large white-ringed black spot on the upper flank and two curving blue lines running down from the eye. Usually seen in pairs feeding on coral polyps.

region: Red Sea & Gulf of Aden
description: Yellow with dark diagonal stripes and a black eye mask followed by a white bar; the Red Sea counterpart of the raccoon butterflyfish. Feeds on coral polyps, algae and small invertebrates, often in pairs.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia & the Philippines to Taiwan & southern Japan
description: White with diagonal grey-brown lines, a large black "panda" patch around the eye and a yellow rear; sold as the Panda Butterflyfish. Feeds on polyps and small invertebrates.

region: Indo-West Pacific — Sri Lanka & the Maldives to New Guinea & the Philippines
description: Resembles the lined butterflyfish, but the black eye bar is broken, leaving an isolated black spot on the nape. Pairs feed on coral polyps, anemones and worms.

region: Indo-Pacific incl. Red Sea — East Africa to Hawaii & the Marquesas
description: The largest butterflyfish: white with thin vertical black lines, a broad black eye bar and a black band sweeping along the rear back. Pairs feed on coral polyps, anemones and small invertebrates.

region: Western Atlantic — New Jersey & Bermuda to Brazil; also off West Africa
description: White with a dark bar through the eye and three broad dark bands on the body, the last crossing the soft dorsal and anal fins. Picks at worm tentacles, coral polyps and small crustaceans.

region: Western Atlantic — Massachusetts & Bermuda to northern South America, incl. Caribbean
description: Grey-white with thin diagonal lines and a large white-ringed black eyespot near the tail, while the real eye is hidden in a dark bar, confusing predators about which way it will flee.

region: Western Atlantic — Massachusetts & Bermuda to Brazil, incl. Gulf & Caribbean
description: White with a black eye bar, yellow fins and a small black spot near the rear tip of the dorsal fin. Pairs patrol shallow reefs picking at worms and polyps.

region: Western Atlantic — North Carolina to Brazil, incl. Gulf & Caribbean
description: Pale yellow-white with a dark eye bar and a broad dark band crossing the rear body, dorsal and anal fins. Usually found on deeper reefs than other Caribbean butterflyfishes.

region: Red Sea & Gulf of Aden
description: Orange-yellow with fine dark horizontal lines and black dorsal, anal and tail fins; also called the Blacktail Butterflyfish. Pairs feed only on coral polyps on Red Sea reefs.

region: Red Sea & Gulf of Aden
description: Blue-grey with fine white chevrons, an orange head and a black rear tail section; also called the Hooded Butterflyfish. An obligate corallivore that picks polyps from Acropora and other stony corals.

region: Central Pacific — Hawaii, Johnston Atoll, the Marshall & Cook Islands
description: A deep-reef species living below about 30 m: white with rows of black dots, a black diagonal upper rear half and a yellow tail. Prized and costly in the trade.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia, the Philippines, Palau & Micronesia
description: White with a black bar through the eye and a broad black band sweeping diagonally from the front of the dorsal fin to the tail. Lives on steep outer-reef walls, usually below about 40 m.

region: Indo-Pacific — Maldives to the Tuamotus & southern Japan
description: Yellow with rows of tiny blue dots, a short blue-black eye bar and a dorsal filament in adults. Usually in pairs on lagoon and channel reefs, feeding on polyps and small invertebrates.

region: Western Pacific — Great Barrier Reef, Lord Howe Island & southern Papua New Guinea
description: Golden yellow with two orange-brown bands edged in blue and a black spot on the tail stalk. Feeds on coral polyps and small invertebrates on Australian reefs.

region: Western Pacific — Gulf of Thailand & southern China to Taiwan & southern Japan
description: Yellow with diagonal orange lines, a black eye bar followed by a white band, and a black blotch on the nape; also called Wiebel's Butterflyfish. Feeds on coral polyps and small invertebrates.

region: Northwest Pacific — Ryukyu, Izu & Ogasawara Islands of Japan
description: Dark charcoal-brown with a pale-edged scale net like wrought iron and yellow fin margins. Endemic to southern Japan and highly prized by collectors.

region: Eastern Indian Ocean & western Pacific — India & Sri Lanka to the Philippines & northern Australia
description: Pale yellow-white with eight thin black vertical bands, one passing through the eye. An obligate coral-polyp feeder of sheltered coastal reefs that seldom thrives in aquaria.

region: Hawaiian Islands
description: A Hawaiian endemic, yellow with diagonal blue stripes, a black spot on the nape and another on the tail stalk. Feeds on worms, crustaceans and coral polyps.

region: Southwest Pacific — eastern Australia & Lord Howe Island to Fiji, Tonga & Pitcairn
description: Dusky brown-black with a yellow snout and face trim and yellow-edged fins; large adults develop a bump on the nape. Feeds on coral polyps, algae and small invertebrates.

region: Northern Australia & southern Papua New Guinea
description: Golden yellow with an orange eye bar and a second orange bar behind it, both edged in blue. Feeds on coral polyps on shallow coastal reefs.

region: Western Indian Ocean — East Africa & Madagascar to Sri Lanka
description: Pale grey-white with faint chevrons, a yellow head and yellow fins. One of the larger butterflyfishes, feeding on polyps, algae and worms.

region: Eastern Pacific — Gulf of California to Peru & the Galápagos
description: The common butterflyfish of the tropical eastern Pacific: white with dark bars through the eye, across the mid-body and at the rear, and a black-banded tail. Feeds on small invertebrates and algae.

region: Eastern Indian Ocean & western Pacific — Andaman Sea to the Great Barrier Reef & southern Japan
description: White with black-edged copper-orange bands, a long tubular snout for probing crevices and a false eyespot on the rear dorsal fin. Famous among reefkeepers for eating pest Aiptasia anemones.

region: Northern Australia, southern New Guinea & eastern Indonesia
description: Like the copperband but with one broad orange band across the body and a dark-edged rear; adults lack the dorsal eyespot. Probes crevices with its long snout for worms and small crustaceans.

region: Southwestern Australia
description: A temperate-water coralfish, white with five dark brown vertical bars (the first through the eye) and a long snout; also called the Western Talma. Probes rocky reefs and sponge gardens for small invertebrates.

region: Indo-Pacific & eastern Pacific — Red Sea & East Africa to Hawaii & Mexico
description: Yellow with a black triangle over the upper head, a white chin and chest, an eyespot below the tail, and an extremely long snout for plucking tube feet, worm tentacles and small crustaceans from crevices.

region: Indo-Pacific — East Africa to Hawaii & the Marquesas
description: Has an even longer, thinner snout than the yellow longnose and rows of small black dots on the chest; a rare all-brown colour phase also occurs. Feeds mostly on small crustaceans picked from crevices.

region: Indo-Pacific — East Africa & the Arabian Gulf to the Society Islands & southern Japan
description: White with two broad black diagonal bands, yellow rear fins and a long white dorsal pennant. Usually in pairs near the reef, picking benthic invertebrates and plankton; often confused with the schooling bannerfish.

region: Indo-Pacific incl. Red Sea — patchy, from East Africa to Hawaii & southern Japan
description: Forms large midwater schools that feed on zooplankton above reef slopes, and sometimes cleans other fishes. Nearly identical to H. acuminatus but with a shorter snout and more rounded anal fin, and generally reef-safe.

region: Indo-Pacific — Andaman Sea to the Pitcairn Islands & southern Japan
description: White with three dark diagonal bands, a yellowish snout and a moderately long dorsal pennant. Feeds largely on coral polyps, so it is not reef-safe.

region: Indo-Pacific — East Africa to the Marquesas & southern Japan
description: Adults grow a short bony horn above each eye; white with a broad black band across the head and another across the body, and yellow rear fins. Usually in pairs, feeding on benthic invertebrates.

region: Indo-Pacific — Maldives to Samoa & southern Japan
description: The largest bannerfish, grey-white with a black eye band, a white bar across the nape, two broad dark bands and a yellow tail; adults have a short horn above each eye. Usually solitary or paired along deep lagoon and channel slopes.

region: Indo-Pacific — Indonesia & the Andaman Sea to the Society Islands & southern Japan
description: Dark brown with thin white lines outlining a triangular pattern; adults develop a bony hump on the nape and short horns above the eyes. Often shelters beneath ledges, feeding on coral polyps and small benthic invertebrates.

region: Red Sea & Gulf of Aden
description: Red Sea endemic with a black eye band, two black diagonal bands, a yellow rear and a shorter dorsal pennant than the longfin bannerfish. Often seen in pairs or small groups feeding on plankton and benthic invertebrates.

region: Pacific & eastern Indian Ocean — Christmas Island to Hawaii & the Pitcairn Islands
description: Forms large schools that feed on zooplankton in open water along drop-offs. A white pyramid-shaped flank patch sits below a yellow back, with a dark brown head.

region: Indian Ocean — East Africa to the Andaman Sea & Java
description: Black front and rear with a broad white vertical band and a yellow spot at the dorsal fin base; also called the Black Pyramid Butterflyfish. Schools in midwater to feed on plankton.

region: Pacific — Hawaii, the Marianas, Samoa & the Society and Line Islands
description: A plain grey-brown planktivore that schools off steep outer reef slopes; one of the least colourful butterflyfishes. Seldom collected for the trade.

region: Eastern Indian Ocean & western Pacific — Andaman Sea to the Great Barrier Reef & southern Japan
description: White with three dark-edged orange-gold bands and a black eyespot on the soft dorsal fin. Usually in pairs on coastal reefs, feeding largely on sponges and small invertebrates.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia, the Philippines, New Guinea & the Solomon Islands
description: White with orange-brown bands and large black eyespots on both the soft dorsal and anal fins. Feeds largely on sponges, living in pairs on steep reef slopes.

region: Western Pacific — Indonesia & the Philippines to the Great Barrier Reef & southern Japan
description: A tall-finned coralfish, white with copper-brown bands; juveniles carry a dorsal eyespot that disappears with age. Lives on silty coastal reefs, feeding on sponges and invertebrates.

region: Eastern Pacific — Gulf of California to Panama & the Galápagos
description: Golden yellow with a black band along the top of the head and back and a black snout. Adults run cleaning stations, picking parasites off other fishes and even hammerhead sharks.

region: Western Atlantic — Florida & the Bahamas to Venezuela, incl. Gulf & Caribbean
description: A small, long-snouted butterflyfish with a dark orange-brown back and pale yellow-white flanks. Lives alone on deeper reefs, plucking tube feet from sea urchins and tentacles from worms.

region: Western Atlantic — Bahamas & Caribbean to the Guianas
description: A deep-reef species: pale yellow with broad dark diagonal bands through the eye and across the body. Rarely collected and seldom seen by divers.

region: Western Atlantic — North Carolina to the Gulf of Mexico & Yucatán
description: A deep-water butterflyfish of offshore banks, pale with a dark eye bar and a dark oblique band from the front of the dorsal fin across the body. Rarely seen shallower than 30 m.

region: Eastern Pacific — Southern California Channel Islands to the Galápagos
description: Golden yellow with a black scythe-shaped band curving from the nape along the back to the soft anal fin. Lives around rocky reefs in cool water, usually below 20 m.

region: Southwest Pacific — Lord Howe & Norfolk Islands, New South Wales & northern New Zealand
description: A subtropical butterflyfish, white with five dark brown vertical bands and yellowish fins. Lives on rocky and coral reefs in cool, subtropical water.

region: Northwest Pacific — southern Japan & Korea to Taiwan, China & the Philippines
description: Formerly Chaetodon modestus: pale with three broad brown bands and a white-ringed black eyespot on the soft dorsal fin. A deep-water species of rocky and coral reefs.

region: Indo-West Pacific — India & Sri Lanka to Fiji, northern Australia & southern Japan
description: Has a tall dorsal fin with only six spines, white with orange-brown bands and a dark eyespot on the soft dorsal. Lives on silty coastal reefs and around seagrass and sponges.
